match.reason: The new point covers dilations, reflections and translations together as one overview, but each bank point teaches only one transformation type, and the Year 12 combining-transformations point goes beyond this Year 11 depth, so no single bank point is the same idea.

draft.title: Transformations of graphs
card: Translation
y = f(x − h) + k moves the graph h units right and k units up. A minus inside the bracket moves the graph right.
Reflection
y = −f(x) reflects the graph in the x-axis. y = f(−x) reflects it in the y-axis.
Dilation
y = a f(x) stretches the graph by a factor of a from the x-axis. y = f(x/b) stretches it by a factor of b from the y-axis.
Each point (x, y) moves in a set way. For example, y = (x + 1)² − 4 is y = x² moved 1 left and 4 down, so its vertex is (−1, −4).
draft.remember: Outside the bracket changes y. Inside the bracket changes x, and in the opposite way to how it looks.

a.q: The graph of y = x² is translated 3 units right and 2 units down. What is the new rule?
a.why: Moving right by 3 means x is replaced by (x − 3), and moving down by 2 means subtracting 2. The option with (x + 3) moves the graph left, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Right 3 puts a minus inside the bracket.

b.q: The point (6, 4) lies on y = f(x). Which point lies on y = −f(x/2)?
b.why: Replacing x with x/2 stretches the graph by a factor of 2 from the y-axis, so x goes from 6 to 12. The negative sign outside reflects in the x-axis, so y goes from 4 to −4. (3, −4) is tempting, but it halves x instead of doubling it.
b.clue: Deal with x and y separately: one is stretched, one is flipped.

final.title: Transformations of graphs
card: Translation
\(y = f(x - h) + k\) moves the graph \(h\) units right and \(k\) units up. A minus inside the bracket moves the graph right.
Reflection
\(y = -f(x)\) reflects the graph in the x-axis. \(y = f(-x)\) reflects it in the y-axis.
Dilation
\(y = af(x)\) stretches the graph by a factor of \(a\) from the x-axis. \(y = f\left(\frac{x}{b}\right)\) stretches it by a factor of \(b\) from the y-axis.
Each point \((x, y)\) moves in a set way. For example, \(y = (x + 1)^{2} - 4\) is \(y = x^{2}\) moved 1 left and 4 down, so its vertex is \((-1, -4)\).
final.remember: Outside the bracket changes \(y\). Inside the bracket changes \(x\), and in the opposite way to how it looks.

a.q: The graph of \(y = x^{2}\) is translated 3 units right and 2 units down. What is the new rule?
a.why: Moving right by 3 means \(x\) is replaced by \((x - 3)\), and moving down by 2 means subtracting 2. The option with \((x + 3)\) moves the graph left, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Right 3 puts a minus inside the bracket.

b.q: The point \((6, 4)\) lies on \(y = f(x)\). Which point lies on \(y = -f\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)\)?
b.why: Replacing \(x\) with \(\frac{x}{2}\) stretches the graph by a factor of 2 from the y-axis, so \(x\) goes from 6 to 12. The negative sign outside reflects in the x-axis, so \(y\) goes from 4 to \(-4\). \((3, -4)\) is tempting, but it halves \(x\) instead of doubling it.
b.clue: Deal with \(x\) and \(y\) separately: one is stretched, one is reflected.

wants.brief: The example on card line 4: y = x^2 dashed and y = (x + 1)^2 - 4 solid, an arrow from (0, 0) to the new vertex (-1, -4), each curve labelled.
notes: The label y = x^2 is drawn in the top-left corner, just above where the solid curve's left branch leaves the graph and well away from the dashed curve (which leaves the top at about x = -2.45), so a student can read it as naming the solid curve; its labelAt of -2.73 puts it at y = 7.45, above the y-axis maximum of 6, so it should be moved to a point on the dashed curve inside the axes, for example on its right branch.
The y-axis runs through the y of the label y = (x + 1)^2 - 4, which starts right on the axis line; move it further right.
The arrow from (0, 0) to (-1, -4) runs into the O at the origin; move the O or leave it out.
